issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: The problem statement (text and UML) declares a method addGuestStudents(int, String) — an int parameter for the number of new guest students plus a String reason — but the solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This parameter-list mismatch (two-parameter signature described vs. one-parameter signature implemented) will confuse students and test harnesses: instructors/tests that expect addGuestStudents(int, String) will not find a matching method in the solution, and students following the UML will implement a different signature than the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make signatures consistent. Option A (preferred if the reason is required by the exercise): change the solution method to match the UML and problem text, e.g. public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; /* optionally handle or store reason */ }. Option B (if the reason parameter was not intended): update the problem statement and UML to declare addGuestStudents(int) only, removing the String reason from the specification so it matches the solution.

issues.description: Method signature mismatch for the addGuestStudents operation: the problem statement and UML declare a method named addGuestStudents with two parameters (addGuestStudents(int, String) — an int for the number of new guest students and a String reason). The template contains only a TODO placeholder for addGuestStudents (no concrete signature) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, and the solution implements addGuestStudents with a single int parameter (public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents)). Because the same method name is used but the parameter lists differ, students cannot unambiguously map the required API from the problem/UML to the implementation, which may lead to confusion about the required signature and how to call or implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent with the problem statement/UML by changing the implementation signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) in both the template and the solution. Preserve the intended behavior of incrementing numberOfGuestStudents (e.g., numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents) and optionally handle or record the reason (for example, log it or add a field/comment). Ensure the method signature in tests/UML, template TODO, and solution all match exactly.
